title: Is forty two divisible by twelve?
description: The primes of twelve are counted against the row of primes of forty two, prime by prime. Keeko doubts this and says two and three are both there so it is divisible.
teaching_notes: One idea: a prime of the divisor must occur in the number as many times as in the divisor. Watch for students who check only which primes appear and not how many times.

source: Is 42 divisible by 12? Find the prime factorisations of both
video_script.why: The child sees that a number is not divisible by another when a prime occurs fewer times in the number than in the divisor.
video_script.substitution: the book's own numbers, forty two and twelve
video_script.anchor: the rows of primes of forty two and twelve, with the two twos of twelve counted against the one two of forty two
video_script.wrong_answer: two and three are both there so it is divisible
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko checks that the primes two and three of twelve appear in forty two, but does not count how many times the two appears.
video_script.payoff_line: Forty two is not divisible by twelve

final_answer.spoken: forty two is not divisible by twelve

maths_rules: 12 needs the prime 2 twice, and 42 has the prime 2 only once
the row of 12 is not included in the row of 42, so 42 is not divisible by 12
video_script.design: The rows of primes of forty two and twelve are lined up. Each prime of twelve is matched with a prime of forty two, and the second two of twelve has none to match.

<bookmark mark='rows'/>Forty two is two times three times seven. Twelve is two times two times three.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Is forty two divisible by twelve?

marks.rule: a number is divisible by another when the primes of the other are all included in its primes

narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>A number is divisible by another when the primes of the other are all included in its primes.
<bookmark mark='twice'/>A prime may be written twice in a row, and then we count it twice.

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the rows of primes of forty two and of twelve.

<bookmark mark='second'/>The second two of twelve has no match.

beats.on_screen: Answer: No, 42 is not divisible by 12

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>No. Forty two is not divisible by twelve. The row of twelve is not included in the row of forty two.

narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble says two and three are both there so it is divisible; the two 2s of 12 are counted against the one 2 of 42; the bubble is struck through in the warning colour

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks two and three are both there so it is divisible.
<bookmark mark='count'/>But twelve needs the prime two twice, and forty two has it only once.
<bookmark mark='strike'/>It is not enough to find the same primes, because we must count how many times.
